solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe that family member supporting sister with nothing to hide

parts.note: a relative is any member of one's family
to be pro something is to support it

indicators.note: the sister is said to conceal the nothing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone praises a relative who backs up their sister, who has nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe that' is the definition: 'that' in 'the man that I saw' is one example of the word class. 'to hide' puts O inside NUN to make NOUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'that' can introduce a relative clause, so it is an example of this grammatical class.

clue.text: Behaviour after game must preclude a row

indicators.note: the game comes first and the trimmed behaviour word follows after it

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: to preclude something is to shut it out, so the a is left out of the behaviour word

parts.note: action means behaviour, how one conducts oneself

explanation.surface: A rule says that conduct after a match must prevent any quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must preclude a' means the behaviour word has to shut out its letter A. RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy quarrel or disturbance, the sense of a row rhyming with 'cow'.

clue.text: Primate is following God for the most part

indicators.note: the word is comes after the shortened God word
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Lord is God

explanation.surface: A churchman, a primate, mostly follows God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop with the God surface, but it is the animal. 'for the most part' cuts LORD to LOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The loris is a small slow-moving nocturnal monkey-like animal of Asia, one of the primates.

clue.text: Doll maybe you distort finally, squeezing body parts

indicators.note: the you and distort pieces press around the body parts, which go inside

parts.note: thee is an old form of you
ears are parts of the body

indicators.note: the last letter of distort is taken

explanation.surface: A toy doll might be distorted by someone squeezing its limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Doll Tearsheet is a prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2. 'squeezing' puts EARS inside THEET, after its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll is the first name of the Shakespearean character with this surname, so she is an example.

clue.text: Base in small community from which convict's escaped

indicators.note: the convict has got out of the village, so those letters leave it

parts.note: a village is a small community
a lag is a convict; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A prison base sits in a village from which an inmate has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from which convict's escaped' takes LAG out of VILLAGE, leaving VILE. 'Lag' is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of morally low or despicable is a synonym for vile.

clue.text: Fastidiousness comes from editor stuck in room

indicators.note: the editor is wedged into the room, so goes inside it

parts.note: a pantry is a room for storing food

explanation.surface: A fussy streak develops in an editor confined to a small room.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with small details and rules, a kind of fussy fastidiousness.

clue.text: Unfashionable game generates cost

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: Playing an old-fashioned game runs up expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgo is money that goes out, an outlay or expenditure.

clue.text: Shout of approval accompanying flowering plants and shrubs

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight
asters are daisy-like flowering plants

explanation.surface: Visitors cheer as they admire a garden of flowers and bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleasters are shrubs or small trees, including the wild olive and Russian olive.

clue.text: Unfortunately, short answer to problem doesn't exist!

indicators.note: things gone wrong are disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the word answer is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sadly, a quick reply to a problem does not exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts ANSWER to ANSWE; with TO those letters are rearranged by 'Unfortunately'. 'short answer' looks like one phrase meaning a curt reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a task is easy, i.e. that there is no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Clipped dog that's made better all round

indicators.note: the made-better word goes round the dog word

parts.note: cured means healed, made better
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A dog that has had its coat clipped was nursed back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the noun, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means cut short, a synonym of clipped.

clue.text: Old Chinese coins left in sofa returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the result reads backwards
the left letter goes inside the sofa word

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: Antique Chinese coins were left down the back of a sofa and given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside SEAT to make SLEAT, which 'returned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Taels were Chinese units of weight used as money, silver currency in former times.

clue.text: Those elected first to make demand

parts.note: the ins are the party in office, those elected
first is written 1st, with I standing for one

explanation.surface: Newly elected representatives first get to make their demands.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the digit 1 often becomes the letter I, so 1ST gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, refusing to take no.

clue.text: At back of witch's place observe one authorised to receive money

indicators.note: the observe word goes at the back of the witch's place

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is consulted by Saul in the Bible
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: Someone at the back of a witch's house watches a person paid to collect money.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsee is the person to whom a cheque or bill is signed over, entitled to its payment.

clue.text: Name given to stranger who offers a cursory greeting?

parts.note: odder means more strange

explanation.surface: We ask what to call an unknown person who barely says hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun, an unknown person, but it is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who merely nods at a passer-by gives the briefest acknowledgement, hence this label.

clue.text: Depression's limiting quiet individual, they'll testify

indicators.note: the depressions hem in the other pieces, which go inside

parts.note: a dent is a depression; read as plural depressions
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A low mood keeps one solitary person quiet, but witnesses will speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood; it is a dent. 'limiting' wraps DENTS around PONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deponents are people who give sworn evidence, as in an affidavit, so they testify.

clue.text: Likelihood of one looking for gold not finding it?

indicators.note: the gold is missing, so those letters go

parts.note: a prospector searches for gold
it refers back to gold, which is or in heraldry

explanation.surface: We ask what chance a gold hunter has of striking nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to gold, OR in heraldry, which is removed from PROSPECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a chance or possibility of something happening, a likelihood.

clue.text: Hat, sort we use in storm?

indicators.note: letters caught in a storm are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: We ask what kind of hat we would wear in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat with a broad back brim, worn by sailors in foul weather.

clue.text: It's always cold, climbing — help not half needed when falling into it!

definitions.text: It's always cold, climbing — help not half needed when falling into it!

indicators.note: the help piece drops into the gap inside the other letters
in a down clue, climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: only half the help word is kept

parts.note: to assist is to help

explanation.surface: A climber in the cold calls for help on falling into a deep crack in the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads EVERC upwards, giving CREVE; 'not half' keeps half of ASSIST; 'falling into it' drops that half into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier, always icy, into which climbers may fall.

clue.text: Old bar staff taking candles across street

indicators.note: the candles stretch across the street, which ends up inside

parts.note: tapers are thin candles

explanation.surface: Former pub workers carry candles over the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapsters were people who drew beer at a tavern, an old term for bartenders.

clue.text: Female voice raised when there's delay

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a female
to voice something is to emit it

explanation.surface: A woman's voice rises at the moment of a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' looks like a noun but is the verb, EMIT; 'raised' turns GALEMIT upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A time lag is an interval of waiting between one event and a related one.

clue.text: Star is attractive but heartless, a "queen"

indicators.note: the central letter is taken away

parts.note: something that pulls draws others to it, so is attractive
R is for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A film star is attractive but cold-hearted, a diva.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle L of PULLS to leave PULS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulsar is a rotating neutron star that emits regular pulses of radio waves.

clue.text: City developer redeveloping our slum

indicators.note: redeveloping rebuilds in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An urban planner is regenerating a run-down area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City developer' looks like a property man; it means the founder of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus is the legendary founder of Rome, so he developed that city.

clue.text: Fellow with dog taken short hangs around good shrub

indicators.note: the fellow and dog pieces hang around the good letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A man with a dog caught short lingers by a nice bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' plays on needing the toilet, but here it trims the dog's name. 'hangs around' wraps the fellow-and-dog letters around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangrove is a tropical tree or shrub that grows in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Kitchen item stuffs centre of marrow with something very cold

indicators.note: the cold thing is packed inside the centre letters
the middle two letters of the word marrow are taken

parts.note: ice is frozen water, very cold

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs a marrow with something frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of a six-letter word is its middle pair of letters, and 'stuffs' puts the cold thing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricer is a kitchen utensil that presses cooked potato or vegetables through small holes.

clue.text: Division brought by hesitation after thirty days

indicators.note: the hesitation comes after the month

parts.note: September has thirty days, abbreviated SEPT
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A split came about through dithering after a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A septum is a dividing wall or partition in the body, as between the nostrils.

clue.text: Publication shows discretion with writer's final piece included

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the discretion word

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with others
the last letter of writer is R

explanation.surface: A published pamphlet shows tact once the author's last section is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political, a kind of publication.

clue.text: The present time offers zilch

parts.note: the present moment is now

explanation.surface: These days, nothing is on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: NOWT is northern English dialect for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zilch is slang for nothing, and this northern dialect word means the same.

clue.text: Nothing written about sort of current needed for scientific apparatus

indicators.note: written about means written around the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Nothing in print concerns the electricity a lab device needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of'; here it reverses NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A linac is a linear accelerator, a machine physicists use to speed up particles.

clue.text: Financial problem posed by brief season

parts.note: brief means short
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A short autumn causes money troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, where money raised falls below what is needed.

clue.text: Awful stir: gent so irate makes complaint after bad meal?

indicators.note: an awful mess is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry diner causes a dreadful fuss in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grumble to the waiter; it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and gut, an ailment often caused by bad food.
